entries.name: Aient
entries.description: AI-native observability: search OpenTelemetry logs, list detected error problems by signature, detect statistical anomalies in error rate/latency/throughput, get a consolidated service-health summary (p50/p95/p99), and synthesize a production incident from a stack trace with an autonomous fix attempt. Pay-per-call via x402 on Base.

usage.callShape: POST https://aient.ai/x402/diagnose with JSON body {service_name, incident}

quirks: inputSchema is undocumented (null in registry) — field names discovered only via 400 error hints
Required fields: service_name (string) AND incident (the stack trace / incident text). The field is named 'incident', NOT 'stackTrace'
Validates input strictly and charges $0.20 per call EVEN on 400 bad_request — a wrong body still costs money. Get the body right before paying

Two paid probes were spent ($0.40 total) discovering required fields: first revealed service_name_required, second revealed incident_required. A successful 2xx was NOT landed within the 2-attempt money-safe ceiling
usage.guide: POST to https://aient.ai/x402/diagnose with a JSON body containing both service_name (the affected service, e.g. 'checkout-api') and incident (the stack trace or incident description text). Pays $0.20 USDC per call via x402 on Base. NOTE: this endpoint charges even for 400 validation errors, so include BOTH required fields on the first call. The /diagnose route synthesizes a production incident from the stack trace and attempts an autonomous fix; read body.success and the result payload. On failure read body.error.message for the missing-field hint.

entries.name: Datadog
entries.description: Access the Datadog monitoring API (metrics, logs, events) metered per call via an x402 pay-per-call gateway (HTTPay) at $0.002 per call — no Datadog account or API key required.

usage.callShape: POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/datadog/api/v1/series with JSON body {series:[{metric,points,type,host,tags}]} — but gateway also requires an X-Upstream-Token header with your own Datadog API key
usage.outputShape: N/A — returns 401 error object: body.error, body.instructions, body.authType ('apikey')
quirks: NOT keyless: registry description ('no Datadog account or API key required') is FALSE.

Charge-then-401: HTTPay gateway accepted the x402 payment ($0.002 settled on Base) THEN returned HTTP 401 demanding an upstream Datadog API key via the X-Upstream-Token header. Money is lost on every call without that key.
Requires the caller's own Datadog API key (authType:apikey) passed as X-Upstream-Token. MasterKey has no such key, so the endpoint is unusable.
Do NOT retry without a real Datadog API key — every attempt charges $0.002 and 401s.
Provider is HTTPay (poweredBy: Alfred Zhang); gateway is x402-enabled but proxies to an auth-gated upstream.
usage.guide: This endpoint is broken for keyless use. The HTTPay x402 gateway charges $0.002 per call and then returns HTTP 401 because the upstream Datadog API requires your own API key passed in the X-Upstream-Token header. Without a Datadog API key the call always fails after taking payment, so do not call it. If a key were available, you would POST {series:[{metric,points:[[unixTs,value]],type:"gauge",host,tags}]} plus header X-Upstream-Token: <datadog-api-key>. The registry claim that no API key is required is incorrect and this endpoint violates the no-API-key policy.

entries.name: Strale Page Speed Test
entries.description: Measures a web page's load performance and Core Web Vitals via the Google PageSpeed Insights API, returning a 0-100 performance score, an A-F grade, metrics (LCP/FCP/CLS/TBT/TTFB/Speed Index) and optimization opportunities for mobile or desktop.

url.description: Page URL to test (e.g. https://example.com) — query param, required

strategy.description: mobile or desktop (default: mobile) — query param, optional

metrics.description: lcp_ms, fcp_ms, cls_score, tbt_ms, ttfb_ms, speed_index

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/page-speed-test?url=<page-url>&strategy=<mobile|desktop> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453; no JSON body; url is a required query param, strategy optional and defaults to mobile)
usage.outputShape: url, strategy, performance_score (0-100), grade (A-F), metrics{lcp_ms,fcp_ms,cls_score,tbt_ms,ttfb_ms,speed_index}, opportunities[], diagnostics[], _meta{capability,latency_ms,provenance{source,fetched_at},payment}
quirks: url and strategy are QUERY PARAMS on a GET request (no JSON body): ?url=<value>&strategy=mobile
strategy defaults to mobile if omitted; accepts 'mobile' or 'desktop'.
Payment is Base USDC only (eip155:8453); the live 402 advertises a single accept — no Solana option here.
Backed by Google PageSpeed Insights (body._meta.provenance.source = 'pagespeedonline.googleapis.com'); latency ~6.5s per call, so budget for a slower response than most Strale ops.
https://example.com scored performance_score 100 / grade A with all Core Web Vitals near zero (empty opportunities/diagnostics).
usage.guide: Measure a web page's load performance and Core Web Vitals. Issue a GET to https://api.strale.io/x402/page-speed-test with a required query param `url` (e.g. url=https://example.com) and an optional `strategy` (mobile or desktop; defaults to mobile). Pay the x402 quote (~$0.054 USDC on Base eip155:8453; no JSON body, no auth beyond x402). On a 200, read body.performance_score (0-100) and body.grade (A-F) for the overall verdict; body.metrics carries the Core Web Vitals (lcp_ms, fcp_ms, cls_score, tbt_ms, ttfb_ms, speed_index) and body.opportunities/diagnostics list optimization suggestions. Data comes from the Google PageSpeed Insights API; expect ~6-7s latency. Plain synchronous JSON response, no async polling.
